subject: PO structuring: annual commit vs usage-based + buyer signoff path
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@midcapanalytics.com>, procurement@midcapanalytics.com
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-15T09:07:00Z
Subject: PO structuring: annual commit vs usage-based + buyer signoff path

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for taking the call yesterday. Per our discussion, I wanted to summarize the two private-offer structures we typically present for customers of your size and outline the approvals your procurement/legal/finance teams will need to sign off.

Option A — 12 month annual committed subscription (recommended if you want predictable unit economics):
- Term: 12 months
- Billing: upfront or quarterly invoiced (Marketplace private offer supports both; buyer must accept offer in AWS console)
- Discount: 40% off list on the usage tier; committed spend of $250k annual
- Advantage: predictable unit cost, easier for capacity planning, eligible for larger committed discount tiers

Option B — Usage-based (pay-as-you-go with volume tiers):
- Term: 12 months (offer still created as 1-year PO)
- Billing: monthly usage-based billing through Marketplace
- Discount: sliding scale — 25% at baseline with step-ups at $X/month thresholds
- Advantage: no cap on consumption; better when usage is uncertain

Key notes for AWS private offer mechanics:
- Private offers are time-limited at acceptance; we can set an acceptance window for buyer admins (we usually set 14 days).
- Buyer acceptance is done via the AWS Marketplace console; procurement will need AWS account admin rights to accept.
- For an invoice flow (rather than immediate card charge), buyer must enable Invoicing in their AWS account; this affects timing of funds and payment terms.

To move forward quickly, can you confirm:
1) Which structure you prefer (A or B)
2) Who in procurement/legal will be the AWS account admin executing acceptance?
3) Any required billing terms (net30/net45) so we can model with finance.

I've attached a redline-friendly PO draft and an internal approval matrix template for your team to fill. If helpful, we can also produce a 3-year amortized pricing sheet (multi-year commit) but that would need an additional procurement approval path.

If you confirm the preferred option I’ll prepare the private offer and include the appropriate acceptance window and billing instructions.

Best,
Naomi

Subject: Re: PO structuring: annual commit vs usage-based + buyer signoff path

Hi Naomi —

Thanks — this is helpful. Quick answers: we are leaning toward Option A (annual commit) for budget predictability, but procurement needs to see a net30 invoice option rather than upfront if possible.

Procurement contact who will execute the acceptance is procurement@midcapanalytics.com (they have admin rights). Legal will want to redline the PO (I attached the procurement mailbox on this thread).

Two quick asks from our side:
- Can you split the PO so the committed spend is tied to a single Marketplace subscription (we have internal tagging needs across projects)?
- If we go net30, can you confirm whether Redwood will hold the private-offer acceptance open for 21 days instead of 14 to allow our internal approvers time?

If you can confirm the net30 flow and 21-day acceptance window, we can proceed to final internal signoff.

Regards,
Sarah
Sarah Jenkins
VP Cloud Platform, MidCap Analytics
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-08-15T16:05:00Z
Subject: Re: PO structuring: annual commit vs usage-based + buyer signoff path

Hi Sarah —

Great — glad to hear Option A is the direction. Answers inline below and next steps: 

- Net30 invoice flow: Yes, we can accommodate net30 via Marketplace invoicing. That requires buyer invoicing to be enabled (procurement noted has admin rights) and Redwood finance signing standard invoice terms. We will mark Net30 on the PO and route the private offer for acceptance; billing will occur monthly with invoice at month-end unless you prefer quarterly invoicing (we can do either).

- Acceptance window: We can extend acceptance to 21 days for this deal. I will include that in the offer metadata and call it out in the email to procurement.

- Subscription split / tagging: We can create the private offer as a single subscription but include SKU-level tags and a billing descriptor that the buyer can use to map to internal cost centers. I’ll ask our onboarding team to propose a tag scheme (we’ll need one tag value from your side for the primary cost center).

Next steps (proposed timeline):
1) I will prepare the private offer (Option A, 12m committed, $250k annual at 40% off) with net30 invoicing and a 21-day acceptance window.
2) Send DocuSign link for the PO redlineed (if legal wants a signature) and post the private offer link in HubSpot.
3) Procurement accepts in AWS console, then Redwood issues first invoice per agreed cadence.

I’ll attach the updated PO and a brief one-pager on the invoice flow for Marketplace (customers often miss the invoicing enablement step).

If that works I’ll aim to send the private offer and DocuSign by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks —
Naomi

Team — forwarding the thread after Naomi drafted the net30 + 21-day window. Two internal asks before we publish the private offer: 

1) Finance approval for net30 on a $250k committed deal. Marcus, can you confirm whether we want to require a 30% prepayment for new enterprise customers in EU or whether our standard is OK here? If finance needs prepay, call that out now so NAomi can present to MidCap.

2) Legal: Vanessa, review the PO redline template for any Marketplace-specific clauses (data retention and subprocessing; MidCap is likely to ask for an audit clause). If you can give a quick green/red / items-to-negotiate list by Monday morning we can keep the 21-day acceptance window.

I recommend we avoid a 3-year amortized commit ask unless Marcus thinks finance can bridge; shorter ask keeps procurement comfortable. Naomi — hold off on sending DocuSign until we get finance/legal checks.

Thanks,
Vivek
